docs.title: Home
docs.text: A fluent, thread-safe Go image processing library with chainable operations.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fluent Interface: Chain multiple operations together naturally
  • Thread-Safe: Safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines
  • High-Quality Processing: Uses Catmull-Rom interpolation for resizing
  • Comprehensive Error Handling: Errors propagate through the chain
  • Multiple Format Support: JPEG, PNG input/output
  • Text Watermarks: Add customizable text overlays with font control

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/TamasGorgics/gopiq

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"

    "github.com/TamasGorgics/gopiq"
)

func main() {
    imageData, err := os.ReadFile("img.jpg")
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error reading image: %v\n", err)
        return
    }

    // Load and process an image with method chaining
    processor := gopiq.FromBytes(imageData).
        Resize(800, 600).
        Grayscale().
        Crop(100, 100, 400, 300).
        AddTextWatermark("© 2025",
            gopiq.WithFontSize(24),
            gopiq.WithPosition(gopiq.PositionBottomRight))

    if processor.Err() != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error: %v\n", processor.Err())
        return
    }

    // Export the result
    resultBytes, err := processor.ToBytes(gopiq.FormatJPEG)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Export error: %v\n", err)
        return
    }

    err = os.WriteFile("output.jpg", resultBytes, 0644)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error writing output file: %v\n", err)
        return
    }

    fmt.Println("Image processed and saved successfully")
}

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: gopiq is designed to be thread-safe and supports concurrent usage out of the box.

docs.title: Safe Concurrent Reading
docs.text:
Multiple goroutines can safely read from the same processor instance. The library uses sync.RWMutex to ensure that read operations do not conflict with write operations.

proc := gopiq.New(image).Resize(800, 600).Grayscale()

// Multiple goroutines can safely call these concurrently:
go func() {
    img, err := proc.Image()
    // Use img...
}()

go func() {
    bytes, err := proc.ToBytes(gopiq.FormatPNG)
    // Use bytes...
}()

docs.title: Clone for Independent Processing
docs.text:
For parallel write operations, you should create independent copies of the processor. The Clone() method creates a shallow copy of the processor that is safe to use in a separate goroutine.

original := gopiq.New(image)

// Each goroutine gets its own independent processor
for i := 0; i < 10; i++ {
    go func() {
        processor := original.Clone().
            Resize(100, 100).
            AddTextWatermark("Processed")
        // Process independently...
    }()
}

docs.title: Concurrent Processing Pattern
docs.text:
Here is a common pattern for processing multiple images in parallel.

func processImagesInParallel(images []image.Image) []*gopiq.ImageProcessor {
    results := make([]*gopiq.ImageProcessor, len(images))
    var wg sync.WaitGroup

    for i, img := range images {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func(index int, image image.Image) {
            defer wg.Done()
            results[index] = gopiq.New(image).
                Resize(200, 200).
                Grayscale()
        }(i, img)
    }

    wg.Wait()
    return results
}

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: gopiq includes advanced performance optimizations that can provide dramatic speed improvements.

docs.title: GrayscaleFast() - Parallel Processing
docs.text:
For large images, use GrayscaleFast() instead of Grayscale():

// Up to 33x faster for large images (1920x1080)
processor := gopiq.New(image).GrayscaleFast()

docs.title: Performance Results (500x500 images on Apple M1 Pro):
docs.text:
• Slow method (At/Set): 7.17ms, 3MB allocations
  • Optimized method: 735μs, 1MB allocations (9.7x faster)
  • Parallel method: 276μs, 1MB allocations (26x faster)

docs.title: Performance Configuration
docs.text:
// Custom performance settings
opts := gopiq.PerformanceOptions{
    MaxGoroutines:            8,     // Limit parallel goroutines
    EnableParallelProcessing: true,  // Enable parallel processing
    MinSizeForParallel:       10000, // Minimum pixels for parallel
}

processor := gopiq.NewWithPerformanceOptions(image, opts)

docs.title: Scalability
docs.text: Parallel Processing Performance (1920x1080 images): - 1 goroutine: 5.87ms - 2 goroutines: 3.11ms (1.9x faster) - 4 goroutines: 1.77ms (3.3x faster) - 8 goroutines: 1.23ms (4.8x faster)

docs.title: Optimization Techniques
docs.text:
1. Direct Buffer Access: Bypasses Go's interface overhead
  2. Parallel Processing: Utilizes multiple CPU cores automatically
  3. Memory Pooling: Reduces garbage collection pressure
  4. SIMD-friendly Operations: CPU-optimized pixel processing
  5. ITU-R BT.709 Grayscale: Professional-grade color conversion

docs.title: gopiq Roadmap
docs.text: This roadmap turns the specification into ordered, verifiable milestones. It is dependency-ordered, not calendar-based; no dates or delivery estimates are implied. All milestones are currently Planned.

docs.title: M0 — Make the repository buildable
docs.text:
Priority: P0 · Requirements: BLD-1–BLD-3

  • Move each standalone example into an independently buildable package/directory, or use an equivalent layout that avoids duplicate main functions.
  • Correct example asset paths and run instructions after reorganizing.
  • Keep generated example output separate from tracked input fixtures.
  • Ensure the CI build/test commands cover the resulting package layout.

Exit criteria: go build ./... and go test ./... both complete successfully, and each documented example can be built independently.

docs.title: M1 — Correct core image processing and guard edge cases
docs.text:
Priority: P1 · Requirements: IMG-1–IMG-5, GRAY-1–GRAY-5, SAFE-1–SAFE-3

  • Fix parallel grayscale indexing for non-zero-origin bounds and subimages.
  • Handle empty images and performance-option edge cases without zero-worker division or invalid pixel access.
  • Verify exact grayscale agreement between sequential and parallel paths, including alpha.
  • Check crop coordinate arithmetic and image-buffer size calculations before use or allocation.
  • Define and test empty-source behavior for crop, resize, grayscale, and watermarking.

Exit criteria: Regression tests cover zero-origin and non-zero-origin images, subimages, empty bounds, alpha, and invalid/overflowing dimensions; invalid inputs report chain errors rather than arithmetic-driven panics.

docs.title: M2 — Make watermark and format behavior match the API
docs.text:
Priority: P1 · Requirements: WM-1–WM-5, FMT-1–FMT-4

  • Implement WithFontPath and deterministic font-source option ordering.
  • Validate nil/invalid watermark options and calculate all positions relative to image bounds.
  • Register GIF decoding in the library and retain an explicit error for unsupported GIF encoding.
  • Add tests for font files, option errors, anchor positions, non-zero bounds, and JPEG/PNG/GIF behavior.

Exit criteria: Every advertised option has observable behavior or is removed; format conversion and errors match the specification.

docs.title: M3 — Resolve clone and concurrency semantics
docs.text:
Priority: P1 · Requirements: CON-1–CON-5

  • Make Go docs, README, tests, and concurrency docs consistently describe Clone as shallow.
  • Document that input and returned images are read-only during concurrent processing.
  • Clarify that individual method calls are synchronized but a multi-call chain is not atomic.
  • Replace or extend the current race test so readers and state-changing operations act on the same processor.

Exit criteria: The public contract is consistent across code and docs, and go test -race ./... covers the stated concurrency guarantee.

docs.title: M4 — Establish reliable quality gates and truthful performance docs
docs.text:
Priority: P1 · Requirements: BLD-4, Q-1–Q-6

  • Move timing comparisons out of regular tests and into benchmarks or a separately invoked tool.
  • Decide whether the unused RGBA pool is worth implementing; remove it and its claims if measurements do not support it.
  • Remove or substantiate SIMD and fixed speedup claims with reproducible benchmark data.
  • Add regression coverage for the requirements in M1–M3.
  • Run build, tests, race detection, vet, lint, and documentation build in CI; retain Go 1.24 as the declared minimum unless the policy is deliberately changed.

Exit criteria: Ordinary tests are correctness-focused and stable across machines; all release-gate checks in the specification pass.

docs.title: M5 — Add streaming I/O and decode limits
docs.text:
Priority: P2 · Requirements: EXT-1, EXT-2

  • Design reader-based construction and writer-based encoding while keeping FromBytes and ToBytes compatible.
  • Add configurable encoded-size, dimension, and total-pixel limits, validating before full decode where possible.
  • Document defaults, limit errors, ownership, and resource behavior.

Exit criteria: Streaming callers avoid mandatory full encoded-buffer copies, and configured decode limits are enforced by tests including oversized and malformed inputs.

docs.title: M6 — Expand transformation and format capabilities
docs.text:
Priority: P2 · Requirements: EXT-3–EXT-5

  • Specify proportional resize fit/fill behavior, including rounding, crop, and upscaling rules.
  • Evaluate rotation, flips, and image watermarks with bounds and alpha-compositing semantics.
  • Assess additional formats independently; implement GIF output only after choosing and documenting palette quantization.

Exit criteria: Each selected feature has a written API contract, pixel-level tests, and documentation before implementation is considered complete.

docs.title: M7 — Optimize measured workloads and support bounded batches
docs.text:
Priority: P3 · Requirements: EXT-6–EXT-8

  • Benchmark representative image sizes and processor counts; tune parallel thresholds based on reproducible results.
  • Consider pooling, fixed-point arithmetic, SIMD, or other specialized paths only when profiling justifies them.
  • Design bounded batch processing with explicit ordering, concurrency, and cancellation semantics.
  • Expand fuzz, platform, and Go-version coverage according to the declared support policy.

Exit criteria: Optimizations show a repeatable benefit without changing specified output semantics, and batch/resource behavior is bounded and tested.

docs.title: Cross-milestone rules
docs.text:
• Fixes must include regression tests and keep error propagation consistent with the chain API.
  • Do not claim an optimization or format is supported until implementation and tests demonstrate it.
  • Avoid calendar commitments until scope and maintainer capacity are known.
  • A release is gated by the acceptance criteria in the specification, not by completion of every future extension.

docs.title: gopiq Specification
docs.text:
Status: Draft implementation target · Scope: Correctness, safety, supported formats, concurrency, verification, and planned extensions

This document defines the intended behavior of gopiq and the acceptance criteria for fixing the gaps found in the repository audit. “Must” and “must not” are requirements; “should” indicates a recommended implementation choice.

docs.title: 1. Goals
docs.text:
gopiq must provide a predictable, chainable image-processing API that:

  • builds and tests as a complete Go module, including its examples;
  • handles ordinary and non-zero-origin image bounds without panicking;
  • reports invalid operations through the processor error chain;
  • has clear, testable format and concurrency guarantees; and
  • makes performance claims only when supported by reproducible measurements.

The existing API and Go 1.24 minimum are retained unless a later versioned change explicitly revises them.

docs.title: 2. Baseline gaps
docs.text:
The following are known discrepancies between the current implementation and the target below:

  • go test -short . passes, but go test -short ./... fails because multiple standalone examples declare main in the same package. The workflow also builds ./....
  • WithFontPath is exposed but watermark rendering does not load a font from that path.
  • Parallel grayscale indexing assumes zero-origin coordinates; some non-zero-origin bounds can produce invalid pixel indexes. Empty images can also reach a zero-worker division for certain performance options.
  • Clone is described as a deep copy in Go documentation but shares the image pointer; tests and concurrency docs currently expect shallow sharing.
  • GIF is described as decodable, but the package does not register the GIF decoder itself.
  • The RGBA pool is not used by processing operations, and current performance documentation makes pooling/SIMD claims that the implementation does not substantiate.
  • TestPerformanceComparison performs timing work as a regular test despite having no performance assertion.

docs.title: 3.1 Build, examples, and documentation
docs.text:
• BLD-1: Every Go package in the module must compile under go build ./... and go test ./....
  • BLD-2: Each standalone example must be in its own package/directory (or an equivalent structure that avoids duplicate main declarations). Example instructions must work from the documented working directory.
  • BLD-3: Building examples must not require running them or writing generated images into tracked fixture locations.
  • BLD-4: The MkDocs site must build with the documented requirements, and the specification and roadmap must be discoverable in its navigation.

docs.title: 3.2 Image operations and bounds
docs.text:
• IMG-1: Crop(x, y, width, height) interprets x and y in the source image's coordinate space. The crop rectangle must have positive dimensions, fit within the source bounds, and be computed without integer overflow. The resulting image has bounds starting at (0, 0).
  • IMG-2: Resize(width, height) requires positive target dimensions and produces a zero-origin image of the requested size. Invalid or unrepresentable buffer sizes must become chain errors rather than arithmetic-driven panics.
  • IMG-3: Operations must support valid images whose bounds do not start at (0, 0), including subimages. Pixel loops must use coordinates or offsets appropriate to the image's actual bounds and stride.
  • IMG-4: Operations on empty bounds must have documented behavior and must not panic. Grayscale operations on an empty image are a no-op that preserves its bounds; operations that need source pixels, such as resizing an empty image, report an error.
  • IMG-5: Processing operations must not mutate the source image in place.

docs.title: 3.3 Grayscale and performance options
docs.text:
• GRAY-1: Grayscale and GrayscaleFast must support arbitrary valid bounds and subimages without out-of-range buffer access.
  • GRAY-2: Both methods must use the same documented BT.709 luma calculation and produce identical pixel values for the same input. For the current 8-bit RGBA implementation, the calculation is uint8(0.2126*R + 0.7152*G + 0.0722*B); output RGB channels are equal and alpha is preserved.
  • GRAY-3: Parallel work must use at least one worker only when there are rows to process, and no more workers than rows or the configured maximum. Empty images must never reach a division by zero.
  • GRAY-4: MaxGoroutines <= 0 uses the documented runtime default. MinSizeForParallel <= 0 means no minimum threshold for a non-empty image; it must not make empty-image processing unsafe. EnableParallelProcessing == false always selects the sequential path.
  • GRAY-5: Default options and threshold behavior must be documented and tested. SetPerformanceOptions must remain safe to call concurrently with processor methods.

docs.title: 3.4 Watermarks
docs.text:
• WM-1: Font-source options are applied in order: the last supplied WithFontPath or WithFontBytes option selects the source. With neither option, the embedded Go font is used.
  • WM-2: WithFontPath must load and parse the requested file. File-read, parse, and face-construction failures must be returned through the processor error chain.
  • WM-3: Empty text, a nil option, a nil color, a non-finite or non-positive font size, non-finite offsets, and an unknown position must produce a processor error rather than a panic or silent fallback. Negative finite offsets remain valid and may move text partly outside the image.
  • WM-4: Named positions are calculated relative to the image bounds, including non-zero Min coordinates. Text outside the destination is clipped by drawing; it is not silently repositioned.
  • WM-5: Watermarking must preserve the source image and must be covered by tests for each anchor, custom fonts, errors, and non-zero-origin bounds.

docs.title: 3.5 Formats
docs.text:
• FMT-1: JPEG and PNG decoding and encoding remain supported and covered by round-trip tests.
  • FMT-2: GIF decoding is supported independently of whether the importing application imports image/gif; the library registers the decoder itself.
  • FMT-3: GIF encoding remains unsupported until a palette-quantization policy is selected. Calls to encode GIF must return a clear error, not imply successful support.
  • FMT-4: FormatFromString, ImageFormat.String, and format comments must agree with the formats actually accepted for decoding and encoding.

docs.title: 3.6 Error handling and size safety
docs.text:
• SAFE-1: Chainable operations preserve the first error and do not continue processing after it. Export methods return that error.
  • SAFE-2: Crop arithmetic and image-buffer size calculations must be checked for integer overflow before use or allocation.
  • SAFE-3: Invalid dimensions and configuration must return errors through the existing API. The library is not required to recover from operating-system out-of-memory termination.
  • SAFE-4: Decoding limits for encoded bytes, dimensions, and total pixels are a planned extension; callers must not be told that untrusted input is resource-bounded until those limits exist.

docs.title: 3.7 Concurrency and cloning contract
docs.text:
To preserve current behavior and avoid an implicit full-image copy, the v1 Clone contract is shallow:

  • CON-1: Clone copies processor state and performance options but shares the current image reference. Go documentation, README, tests, and concurrency docs must say this; they must not call it a deep copy or promise independent backing pixels.
  • CON-2: Processing operations treat their input image as read-only and create a new destination. Clones can therefore process the shared source independently as long as the source is not externally mutated.
  • CON-3: Methods on one processor must be internally race-safe. Individual calls are synchronized, but a multi-call chain is not an atomic transaction and may interleave with calls from another goroutine.
  • CON-4: Image() returns the current image for reading. The caller must treat it, and images passed to constructors, as read-only while the processor or its clones may be used concurrently. Mutating an image through a concrete-type assertion is outside the thread-safety guarantee.
  • CON-5: Race tests must exercise concurrent reads and state-changing calls on the same processor, not only writes to separate clones.

If independent pixel storage is later needed, it should be provided by an explicitly named deep-copy API rather than changing the meaning of Clone silently.

docs.title: 3.8 Tests, CI, and performance claims
docs.text:
• Q-1: CI must build and test all packages, run the race detector, and include go vet and the configured linter. It must build the documentation site.
  • Q-2: Tests must cover non-zero-origin images, subimages, empty bounds, alpha preservation, grayscale equivalence, invalid sizes/options, font-path loading, and the declared format behavior.
  • Q-3: Timing comparisons belong in Go benchmarks or a separately invoked performance tool, not ordinary unit tests. Unit tests must not depend on machine speed.
  • Q-4: Benchmark results must include enough environment and workload detail to be reproduced. Documentation must not present old measurements as universal guarantees.
  • Q-5: Pooling or SIMD optimizations may be claimed only when the implementation uses them and reproducible benchmarks demonstrate a benefit. Otherwise, unused pool code and unsupported claims should be removed.
  • Q-6: The supported Go-version policy must be explicit. CI must test the module's declared minimum (currently Go 1.24) and, when selected, the latest supported stable version.

docs.title: 4. Planned extensions
docs.text:
These are not prerequisites for the correctness milestones above; they are future capabilities to consider and scope separately.

  • EXT-1 — Streaming I/O: Add reader-based construction and writer-based encoding so callers need not hold the entire encoded image in a byte slice. Existing byte APIs remain supported wrappers.
  • EXT-2 — Decode limits: Add configurable limits for encoded input size, width, height, and total pixels, with validation before full decode where possible.
  • EXT-3 — Aspect-ratio operations: Add explicit fit/fill or proportional-resize APIs with documented rounding, cropping, and upscaling behavior.
  • EXT-4 — Additional operations: Consider rotation, flips, and image watermarks with clear bounds, anchor, and alpha-compositing behavior.
  • EXT-5 — Additional formats: Consider GIF encoding only with an explicit quantization policy; assess additional formats and dependencies independently.
  • EXT-6 — Bounded batch processing: Consider a worker-pool API with bounded concurrency, ordering guarantees, and cancellation behavior for batch workloads.
  • EXT-7 — Benchmark-led optimization: Profile representative workloads before adding pooling, fixed-point arithmetic, SIMD, or other specialized paths. Keep a simple correct fallback.
  • EXT-8 — Expanded assurance: Add fuzzing for malformed image data and options, broader platform/version CI, and automated checks that documentation examples stay compilable.

docs.title: 5. Release acceptance gate
docs.text:
A release implementing the corrective requirements is ready when all of the following hold:

  1. go build ./... and go test ./... pass.
  2. go test -race ./..., go vet ./..., and the configured linter pass.
  3. The MkDocs site builds and all example instructions work as written.
  4. Requirements in sections 3.2–3.8 have regression tests or an explicit documented exception.
  5. Performance documentation describes measured behavior without unsupported guarantees.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This section covers the core methods for creating and managing ImageProcessor instances.

  • New(img image.Image) *ImageProcessor - Create processor from image
  • FromBytes(data []byte) *ImageProcessor - Create processor from image bytes
  • Clone() *ImageProcessor - Create independent copy
  • Image() (image.Image, error) - Get current image
  • ToBytes(format ImageFormat) ([]byte, error) - Export to bytes
  • Err() error - Get any error from the processing chain

docs.title: Processing Operations
docs.text:
These methods are chainable and perform image manipulation.

  • Resize(width, height int) - Resize using Catmull-Rom interpolation
  • Crop(x, y, width, height int) - Crop to specified rectangle
  • Grayscale() - Convert to grayscale
  • GrayscaleFast() - Convert to grayscale using parallel processing for a significant speed boost.
  • AddTextWatermark(text, ...options) - Add text watermark

docs.title: Watermark Options
docs.text:
Use these functional options to customize text watermarks.

  • WithFontSize(size float64) - Set font size
  • WithColor(color color.Color) - Set text color
  • WithPosition(pos WatermarkPosition) - Set position
  • WithOffset(x, y float64) - Set offset from position
  • WithFontBytes(data []byte) - Use custom font
